stemMd: Two linear pricing plans are $A(h)=20+8h$ and $B(h)=44+5h$. Which choice gives the complete set of positive numbers of hours for which plan A is cheaper?
explanationMd: Solve 20+8h<44+5h: 3h<24, so h<8. Combine with the stated positive-hour domain. At eight hours both cost 84 dollars.

distractorRationale.d: Beyond the crossing, plan A has the larger hourly rate and costs more.
distractorRationale.c: This is only a proper subset of the hours for which plan A is cheaper, so it is not the complete solution set.
distractorRationale.a: At eight hours the plans are equal, not strictly cheaper.
